title: Neural imaging screen detects cardiotoxicity signals in human-derived heart cells
summary: A ResNet50 image model screened human induced-pluripotent-stem-cell-derived cardiomyocytes for compound-associated toxicity signals. Follow-up mitochondrial-respiration assays supported cell-level liabilities for selected screen hits that simple staining measurements had missed. A further comparison separated proteasome inhibitors with similar biochemical potency but different neural toxicity scores. These are in vitro safety signals, with the core results already present in the March2021 preprint; they do not establish human cardiac risk or clinical safety.
ai_technology: ResNet50 convolutional neural network on the PhenoLearn platform
organization: Tenaya Therapeutics; Stanford University; Dana Solutions

evidence.tested: Original preprint and journal Methods describe image-based training/validation and a separate validation plate, screening1280 bioactive compounds plus1280 diverse compounds. Selected hits underwent secondary mitochondrial-respiration assays; proteasome activity was measured for a ten-inhibitor comparison. The cell experiments support the bounded measured result, beyond recovery of known liabilities alone.
evidence.unknown: Cell-line/model-specific in vitro results; technical replicates and model-development validation are not independent clinical replication. Unknown-target-library hits remain phenotypic signals. Human exposure, arrhythmia risk and therapeutic safety were not established; no novel chemical toxicity mechanism is claimed.
evidence.ai_role: A ResNet50 learns staining-image patterns from control and known-toxic conditions, produces a phenotypic toxicity score for screening compounds, and prioritizes hits for orthogonal cell assays.

source_review.scope: Original bioRxiv v1 full JATS Methods/Results, primary history API; corresponding eLife PMC full JATS model Methods, selected-hit orthogonal validation and proteasome comparison. First public core result dated2021-03-24; journal publication2021-08-02. No priority beyond located versions claimed.
